indicators.name: Anomalous IT to OT Network Traffic
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous IT to OT Network Traffic
id: d8f9b1c2-a3e4-4d5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b
status: experimental
description: Detects network traffic crossing from a typical IT network segment to an OT network segment. This is a general hunting rule based on the recommendation to monitor for unexpected traffic between IT and OT networks, as mentioned in the context of a maritime cyber incident. The IP ranges used are placeholders and must be adapted to the specific environment.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/09/daily-ot-security-news-september-19-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-20
tags:
  - attack.lateral_movement
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate, but un-baselined, IT/OT communication.
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    src_ip|cidr: 
      - '192.168.0.0/16' # Placeholder for IT network range
      - '10.0.0.0/8'       # Placeholder for IT network range
    dst_ip|cidr: 
      - '172.16.0.0/12'    # Placeholder for OT network range
  filter_known_good:
    dst_port:
      - 502   # Modbus
      - 44818 # EtherNet/IP
      - 102   # Siemens S7
  condition: selection and not filter_known_good
indicators.description: Detects network traffic crossing the IT/OT boundary that is not explicitly allowed, which could indicate lateral movement from a compromised IT system to critical operational technology. This is a general hunting rule based on threat intelligence.
